translations.translatedText: # Friday 8.6.2018 (radio)

The commanders of the armed forces of the USA and Russia met in Finland. Almost half of Finns want to reject the health and social care reform. The Mediterranean threatens to turn into a plastic sea. The Swedish royal court celebrated a christening.
## Military leaders met in Finland

![The commander of the US armed forces, General Joseph F. Dunford Jr., and the commander of the Russian armed forces, General of the Army Valery Gerasimov.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10241999)
Open image viewer
The commander of the US armed forces, General Joseph F. Dunford Jr., and the commander of the Russian armed forces, General of the Army Valery Gerasimov. Photo: AOP and Lehtikuva
The commanders of the armed forces of the USA and Russia have met in Finland.
The commander of the US army, Joseph Dunford Junior, and Russia's Valery Gerasimov held talks at the Government's representative residence, Königstedt, in Vantaa.
The topics of the talks were not announced in advance, but the commanders have discussed Syria, at least.
The purpose of the meeting is to strengthen trust between Russia and the United States.
The commanders also met President Sauli Niinistö and the commander of the Finnish Defence Forces, General Jarmo Lindberg.
## Support for the health and social care reform is crumbling
![Juha Sipilä at the opening of the Centre Party congress in Sotkamo.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10245637)
Open image viewer
Prime Minister Juha Sipilä defended the health and social care reform at the Centre Party congress in Sotkamo. Photo: Martti Kainulainen / Lehtikuva
Almost half of Finns want to reject the health and social care reform. The health and social care reform means the reform of social and health services.
In a survey by Alma Media's newspapers, only about 20 percent of respondents supported the government's health and social care reform. About 30 percent could not say what they think about the matter.
Support for "sote" is strongest in the Centre Party. Almost half of Centre Party members support the reform. Less than 30 percent of National Coalition Party supporters support the reform.

The Centre Party and the National Coalition Party both hold their party congresses this weekend. The Centre Party is meeting in Sotkamo and the National Coalition Party in Turku. The health and social care reform will certainly be discussed a lot at both meetings.
## Tourism adds plastic waste in the Mediterranean
![Plastic waste floating in the sea](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10199226)
Open image viewer
There is a lot of plastic waste and microplastic in the Mediterranean. Photo: AOP
The Mediterranean threatens to turn into a plastic sea, says the environmental organisation WWF.

Large pieces of plastic waste, such as plastic bags and plastic packaging, float in the Mediterranean. There is also a great deal of microplastic in the Mediterranean, that is, plastic particles so small that they cannot even be seen.
WWF says that all Mediterranean sea animals have microplastic in them. Almost all animals have also eaten large pieces of plastic waste.

WWF says that the increase in plastic waste is caused by tourism. Over 200 million people travel to the Mediterranean countries every summer. Most of the plastic waste comes from Turkey and Spain, WWF says.
Today is World Oceans Day.
## The little Swedish princess was named
![Princess Adrienne.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10244079)
Open image viewer
Adrienne Josephine Alice. Photo: Christopher O'Neill
A christening has been held at the Swedish royal court.
The daughter of Princess Madeleine and Chris O'Neill was given the name Adrienne Josephine Alice.
The christening ceremony of the little princess was held at Drottningholm Church in Stockholm.
Adrienne was born in March. She has a 4-year-old big sister, Leonore, and a 2-year-old big brother, Nicolas.
